summary: The sample runs and demonstrates the required end-to-end refill flow against a reachable Azure DocumentDB cluster: it looks up prescriptions, evaluates eligibility, writes a refillRequest and persists simple agent memory so follow-ups resolve. The builder resolved the Beanie/Node mismatch by implementing the sample in Node.js with Mongoose and a small, rule-based agent; this is documented in README and recorded in decisions.jsonl. Most functional requirements from the prompt are present and were exercised against the live cluster during verification. Several gallery-quality and production best-practice items are missing or only partially implemented (atomic updates/transactions, projection to limit RU, TTL for memory, CI-friendly offline tests, a /search endpoint and search behavior). Those are not fatal for a demo but should be fixed before publishing the gallery sample.

requirement_results.requirement: A single Node.js LangChain agent, built with Beanie ODM — handles the patient's refill request conversationally and decides which of its tools to call as the conversation proceeds.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agent.js lines 10-18 (Agent class present) and README.md line 13 (rule-based agent), but Beanie was not used and LangChain was not integrated.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either change the starter prompt to allow a Node.js ODM (Mongoose) or run the sample in Python with Beanie. For repository-level fix: update the README and starter prompt to request 'an agent implemented in Node.js using Mongoose (or a Node ODM)' instead of Beanie.

requirement_results.requirement: A tool looks up the patient's active prescriptions in Azure DocumentDB through Beanie ODM (e.g. by the patient's identifier and whether the prescription is active) and returns them to the agent.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agent.js lines 56-61 perform Prescription.findOne({ patientId, active: true, drugName: ... }). This performs the lookup, but it uses Mongoose (Node) not Beanie (Python).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If Beanie must be used, reimplement the data-access tool in Python; otherwise change the prompt to allow Node.js + Mongoose and note this substitution in the sample README (already done).

requirement_results.requirement: A tool checks a prescription's refill eligibility from its days supply remaining and its refill count and returns the result to the agent.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agent.js lines 74-78 compute daysRemaining and eligible and lines 80-82 return the ineligible message.

requirement_results.requirement: A tool creates a refill request document in Azure DocumentDB through Beanie ODM for the prescription being refilled.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agent.js lines 85-92 create a RefillRequest and call rr.save(); implemented via Mongoose, not Beanie.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either implement the write with Beanie (Python) or accept Node+Mongoose in the prompt. For atomicity, prefer performing the create + decrement inside a transaction or using an atomic guarded update (see next requirement fix).

requirement_results.requirement: Agent memory keeps context across turns so that a follow-up such as 'refill my blood pressure medication' resolves to the patient's prescription without the patient naming the drug again.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agent.js lines 42-47 (check AgentMemory.findOne) and 68-72 (findOneAndUpdate to persist lastMedication). Model: app/src/models/AgentMemory.js lines 3-6.

requirement_results.requirement: The agent completes a refill by using these tools together: it looks up the prescription, checks its eligibility, and creates the refill request document when the prescription is eligible.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agent.js lines 56-96 show the flow: lookup, eligibility check, create refillRequest, decrement refillCount.

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.js lines 4-8 read process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI; app/.env.example lists a placeholder DOCUMENTDB_URI (app/.env.example line 2).

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example lines 2-5 list DOCUMENTDB_URI, PORT and OPENAI_API_KEY placeholders.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: The sample does not create or use any vector indexes or embeddings; no vector-index code present.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If embeddings are added, include a README section that states the embedding model and its dimensionality and create the vector index with the matching dimension.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector indexes present in the repository; vector-index guidance absent.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If vector search will be part of the sample, add an index creation script and README notes that explain the sample's chosen index type/params and how to retune them.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.js lines 23-30 implement an isConnected guard and return mongoose.connection, so connect() reuses the same connection pool.

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/scripts/seed.js lines 12-14 create indexes; lines 50-52 perform updateOne(..., { upsert: true }) or (in alternate seed file) use findOne/create guard — the seed is idempotent.

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: No /search endpoint exists in app/src/index.js; only POST /chat is implemented (app/src/index.js lines 11-16).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add an explicit /search API that validates the input and returns clear, documented error codes for empty queries and embedding failures (or document that the sample does not include embedding-based search).

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: No search endpoint or embedding-based search present in the codebase.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If adding embedding-based search, return similarity score in the API response and document the format in README and the API contract.

requirement_results.evidence: This is a Node.js project; it includes package-lock.json (app/package-lock.json) which records exact resolved dependency versions for reproducible installs.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: scripts/test-eligibility.js connects to the real DB using connect() (scripts/test-eligibility.js lines 1-7) and is not a mocked unit test. No mock-based unit tests present.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add unit tests using an in-memory MongoDB (mongodb-memory-server) or mock the Mongoose models so tests run offline; add test instructions to README.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No IaC (Bicep/ARM/Terraform) files are present in the repository. The README instructs users to use an existing cluster.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If the gallery wants to include IaC, add a Bicep/ARM/Terraform snippet (Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters) and sample parameters describing tier, storage and region. Otherwise document explicitly that the sample uses an existing cluster and show how to provision one if desired.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: README.md contains what the sample shows and Quickstart setup/run (README.md lines 15-25 and lines 27-34) but lacks explicit clean-up instructions.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a 'clean-up' section to README that shows how to remove created documents/collections or guidance to drop the sample database 'sample_healthcare_15' with a CLI command.

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: README.md line 1 and other places consistently use 'Azure DocumentDB'.

checks.practice: Use a single process-wide MongoClient / Mongoose connection (singleton) and reuse it rather than creating a new client per request.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js lines 23-30 implement isConnected and reuse mongoose.connection.

checks.practice: Always connect with TLS enabled (tls=true) and do not disable certificate verification in production; Azure DocumentDB requires TLS.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example line 2 includes tls=true in the example URI and app/src/db.js reads DOCUMENTDB_URI (app/src/db.js line 4).
checks.source: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Node.js

sources.title: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Node.js

checks.practice: Tune connection-pool parameters according to your environment: small pools for serverless, larger pools for long-running OLTP servers, and set sensible timeouts.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js lines 11-21 set maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS and serverSelectionTimeoutMS.

checks.practice: Limit returned fields (use projection) and keep documents small because request charge (RU) correlates with document size.
checks.evidence: app/src/agent.js lines 56-61 call Prescription.findOne(...) without projections, pulling all fields.
checks.source: Performance tips for Azure Cosmos DB and .NET SDK v2
checks.fix: Return only needed fields (e.g., drugName, daysSupply, refillCount, lastFilledAt) in the find/query; e.g. Prescription.findOne(query, { drugName:1, daysSupply:1, refillCount:1, lastFilledAt:1 })

sources.title: Performance tips for Azure Cosmos DB and .NET SDK v2

checks.practice: Make seed scripts idempotent (use upsert / create-if-not-exists) so they can be safely re-run.
checks.evidence: app/scripts/seed.js lines 50-52 use updateOne(..., { upsert: true }) (or insert-if-not-exists in alternate seed) to avoid duplicates.

checks.practice: When designing an agent's persistent memory collection, plan for lifecycle (TTL or retention) and encryption, and avoid storing full PHI in cleartext agent memory.
checks.evidence: app/src/models/AgentMemory.js lines 3-6 define lastMedication and updatedAt but do not create a TTL index or document retention policy.
checks.fix: Add a TTL index on updatedAt (and document retention guidance) and avoid storing full PHI; store only a canonical drug id where possible. Example: AgentMemory.collection.createIndex({ updatedAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 60*60*24 }) and document retention policy in README.

checks.practice: When creating refillRequest docs and updating prescriptions, decrement refill counts and use single-partition transactions or application-level guarded updates to avoid lost updates.
checks.evidence: app/src/agent.js lines 84-96 create the RefillRequest (rr.save()) and then decrement prescription.refillCount and prescription.save() without a transaction or guarded single-update.
checks.source: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: Perform an atomic guarded update or a single-partition transaction: use findOneAndUpdate with a conditional filter (e.g., { prescriptionId, refillCount: { $gt: 0 } }) and $inc on refillCount, or start a session and run both operations in a transaction with patientId as the partition key.

sources.title: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Use an explicit index on prescriptionId (unique) and patientId + drugName compound index to support fast lookups used by the agent.
checks.evidence: app/scripts/seed.js lines 12-14 create prescription indexes ({ patientId:1, active:1 } and unique prescriptionId) but do not create a compound patientId+drugName index which would speed lookups by patient+drug.
checks.fix: Create an additional compound index: Prescription.collection.createIndex({ patientId:1, drugName:1 }) (or patientId:1, drugName:1, nextRefillDate:-1 if sorting by nextRefillDate is required).

checks.practice: Use explain('executionStats') / the MCP tools to verify index usage and query plans and rework indexes accordingly.
checks.evidence: No calls to explain() or MCP explain_operation are present in the repository and the seed/test tools do not capture explain output; events.jsonl shows the query-optimizer skill was available but not used to run explain() against the created queries.
checks.fix: Add a test/CI script that runs explain('executionStats') for the agent's critical queries (prescription lookup, eligibility filters) and stores or prints the plan and key metrics.

checks.practice: Unit tests run without a live cluster (mocked or in-memory).
checks.evidence: scripts/test-eligibility.js (scripts/test-eligibility.js lines 1-8) connects to the live DB; no mock-based test suite is present.
checks.searched: Searched the repo for test frameworks and in-memory DB usage; found only test-eligibility.js requiring a live connection.
checks.fix: Add unit tests using an in-memory MongoDB (mongodb-memory-server) or mock Mongoose models; update CI instructions and README to show how to run tests offline.

decision_reviews.comment: Decision D001 (approved build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps') appears in decisions.jsonl but there is no corresponding log_decision event in events.jsonl that records D001. The event trace contains other approval entries (D008) and many log_decision calls, but not D001; I could not verify the recorded evidence for D001 in events.jsonl.

D002 (chose Node.js with Mongoose instead of Python+Beanie) is supported by events.jsonl: a log_decision call recorded this choice and the codebase uses Mongoose (app/src/models/* and package.json). The readiness report noted the Beanie/Node mismatch and the implementation follows that decision (evidence events.jsonl entries at timestamp ~08:49:40 and source files).

D003 (chose Mongoose) is recorded in events.jsonl and the code uses Mongoose (package.json and src/models). The reason_source field is 'model_default' (a choice), and the trace shows the change was performed (files created/overwritten).

D004 (read connection string from DOCUMENTDB_URI) is recorded in events.jsonl and implemented in app/src/db.js lines 4-8. The event trace includes a log_decision for D004 and the code reads the env var as stated.

D005 (use existing cluster and do not provision resources) is recorded in events.jsonl and matches the run policy and README. The build used the provided DOCUMENTDB_URI and did not attempt provisioning, consistent with the decision.

D006 states 'I chose a simple in-process conversation memory', but the final code persists memory to a DB collection (app/src/models/AgentMemory.js and app/src/agent.js lines 68-72 use AgentMemory.findOneAndUpdate and AgentMemory.findOne). That contradicts D006; the later decision D011 documents the DB-backed memory choice and is the one actually implemented.

D007 records the choice to implement a small rule-based agent rather than a full LangChain dependency. The repository contains a rule-based Agent (app/src/agent.js) and README documents the choice (README.md lines 12-14). events.jsonl records D007.

D008 (another approval entry) appears in decisions.jsonl but there is no explicit matching log_decision event for D008 in events.jsonl, so I could not verify the event trace for this exact decision id.
D009 duplicates the D002 decision (Node.js + Mongoose); events.jsonl contains a log_decision that recorded D009 and the codebase reflects the choice, so the decision is supported by the trace.
D010 (use env var for connection string) is logged and implemented (app/src/db.js reading DOCUMENTDB_URI). The event trace contains the corresponding log_decision entry.

D011 (DB-backed agent memory in 'agent_memory' collection) is recorded in events.jsonl and implemented in code (app/src/models/AgentMemory.js and app/src/agent.js lines 44-72). The event trace includes the decision and file writes that create the model.
D012 (rule-based agent default, pluggable to OpenAI) is recorded and matches the code (agent is rule-based and README documents how to plug an LLM). events.jsonl contains the log_decision for D012.

D013 (create indexes prescriptions {patientId:1, active:1}, prescriptionId unique, refillRequests {patientId:1, requestedAt:-1}) is recorded and present in app/scripts/seed.js lines 12-14; events.jsonl records the decision and seed was run successfully.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The starter prompt and repository contain no statement of which embedding model (provider and specific model) to use and therefore no guidance that ties embedding dimensionality to the vector-index dimensions or how to set the index accordingly.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Inspected repository (no embedding code) and searched installed skills (documentdb-vector-search) and Microsoft Learn (vector search docs) via learn_microsoft_docs_search.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample did not implement any vector-index or embedding-based features (the builder left vector search out of the demo). Without explicit model/dimension guidance a later contributor may create a mismatched vector index that fails or degrades recall/latency.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short page titled 'Choosing embeddings and vector-index dimensions for Azure DocumentDB' that includes: 1) recommended embedding providers and example models (OpenAI ada/xxx, Azure OpenAI text-embedding-3-small/large, etc.) and their dimensionality; 2) example createIndexes JSON for DiskANN/HNSW/IVF using that dimensionality; 3) a matrix advising which index kind to use for demos vs medium vs large corpora; 4) a short 'how to change the index dimension' subsection for the sample's seed script and README.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The prompt asked for 'Beanie ODM' together with Node.js, a cross-language mismatch. There is no prominent guidance telling builders what to do when the starter prompt requests an ODM that exists only in a different language.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Readiness report, repository, and skills. Searched docs for Beanie references and for guidance about choosing an ODM for Node samples.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder made a pragmatic substitution (Mongoose) and documented it in README. Without clear guidance agents or builders may blindly attempt an impossible combination or choose an inconsistent stack.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'ODM guidance for cross-language prompts' rule to the agent-kit: when a starter prompt names an ODM not available in the requested runtime, prefer the native ODM for that runtime and document the substitution in README and in the decisions log. Example language: 'If the prompt requests Beanie for a Node.js sample, substitute Mongoose and record the decision.'

doc_gaps.topic: Explain() / MCP explain usage for index verification
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Although the query-optimizer skill documents explain() and MCP tools, the sample does not include a developer workflow that runs explain('executionStats') for the agent's critical queries (prescription lookup, eligibility check).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Inspected repository (no explain() calls) and the documentdb-query-optimizer skill.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: No deterministic check that the created indexes actually cover the sample queries; developers may ship an index that does not prevent COLLSCANs or high docExamined counts.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Ship a small 'verify-indexes.js' script (or extend scripts/test-eligibility.js) that runs explain('executionStats') for the sample's key lookups and prints totalKeysExamined / totalDocsExamined / executionTimeMillis; document how to interpret the output in README.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The repository lacks unit tests that run without a live DocumentDB cluster (no in-memory or mocking strategy provided).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Inspected repository (scripts/test-eligibility.js uses real DB) and README (no offline test instructions).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Continuous integration and quick local validation are harder; contributors must have access to an Azure cluster to run tests.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a 'tests' folder with unit tests that mock Mongoose models (or use mongodb-memory-server) and update README with instructions to run tests locally and in CI. Include an example GitHub Actions workflow that runs tests using the in-memory server.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The sample uses a DB-backed agent memory collection but does not create a TTL index or document retention policy or give guidance about PHI storage/encryption for memory.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Inspected app/src/models/AgentMemory.js and README; searched documentdb-indexing and documentdb-security skills.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Agent memory may grow without bound and may store medication identifiers in cleartext without documented retention or encryption guidance.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short subsection to README: 'Agent memory retention & PHI handling' that shows how to create a TTL index, how to store only canonical identifiers instead of detailed PHI, and what disclaimers to include. Also add a sample seed/upgrade script that creates the TTL index: AgentMemory.collection.createIndex({ updatedAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: <n> }).
